question: Regulation (EU) 2024/19381 on standards of quality and safety for substances of human origin (SoHO) applies from 7 August 2027. According to the Czech State Institute for Drug Control, existing SoHo establishments will be deemed authorised as such and newly regulated entities have until November 2027 to register.

In addition, SoHO collected before the date of application may continue to be used under previous rules until August 2029. However, human breast milk has a much shorter shelf life than other SoHOs such as haematopoietic cells or tissues. Depending on the storage temperature, it lasts only three to six months.

The transitional provision for previously collected SoHO therefore offers little practical relief to human milk banks. Many of these, often small hospital-based facilities, may be unable to meet the new equipment and testing requirements by 7 August 2027. 1.
Does the Commission consider that the current transitional provisions adequately address the specific situation of human milk banks?
Does it envisage a specific transitional period or other forms of flexibility for breast milk, for instance through guidance or implementing acts?
How will it support Member States and milk banks in adapting to the new standards so that the supply of donor milk to vulnerable newborns is not disrupted?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1938 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 on standards of quality and safety for substances of human origin intended for human application and repealing Directives 2002/98/EC and 2004/23/EC, OJ L, 2024/1938, 17.7.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1938/oj. 1
